What the speaker said was very true. I believe that the more connected we are, the more alone we feel. This is not a big problem for my generation because we lived without technology for a long time. We know how to be alone and that it is OK to be alone. But for people under 20, it is different. They are always communicating and may never feel alone. They might not learn how to enjoy being by themselves. Also, they are learning to talk through messages that can be changed, instead of learning how to have real conversations with people face to face.

Your dreams might show you all kinds of insights into things that you didn't realise you were thinking about. Common dreams like being able to fly or falling, your teeth falling out or having no clothes on in a public place probably mean something similar in most people. But the key to understanding exactly what they mean to you is to connect them to the events and feelings in your daily life.

One of the most interesting cases of wild animals living in a city are the wild dogs of Moscow. In Moscow, there are approximately 35,000 wild dogs living on the streets. Some of the dogs were born wild, while others are pets that have been abandoned by their owners. Some dogs live alone and others live in packs. In 2010, scientists studied the dogs and found that the dogs have adapted remarkably successfully to urban life. They have learned that it is safer to cross the street with people and some dogs appear to understand traffic lights.

Wonder is New Yorker RJ Palacio's first novel. On her website, she explains that the idea for the book came to her after seeing a girl with facial deformities on the street one day. Wonder has been a bestseller in the United States and has already won several awards. Many schools are using it as a starting point for discussions about bullying, friendship and what it's like to be different. A film version is being made, and many, including me, are waiting eagerly to see what RJ Palacio writes next.

Chloe has two pet rats, Zena and Roxy. Chloe knows they're not typical pets and she has lost count of the times she's patiently tried to explain to people that rats aren't dirty and they make fantastic pets if you look after them correctly. But she understands why people react badly. She didn't like rats either until her friend Martin showed her his pet rats and she saw how affectionate and intelligent they were. Last year, when one of Martin's rats had babies, Chloe decided she'd like to have two of them.

Cape Town can be a dangerous place for baboons. Some have been hurt or killed in car accidents, and others have died from electric shocks while playing with wires. Baboons are an endangered species, so to protect them and reduce problems between people and baboons, the city council has hired a team of Baboon Monitors. Their job is to move baboons away from the city or catch them and release them in the countryside. This plan has worked somewhat, but it is difficult to stop baboons from returning to the city when they find easy food there.

I work for a global IT company, but their main office is in the United States, so I do all my work online from home. This means I don't spend time commuting or chatting with coworkers. I work on different projects, and this flexibility is very important to me. It allows me to take time off when my children have school performances or when I need to go to the dentist. The downside is that without set office hours, I often work late into the evening and sometimes skip dinner to finish my tasks.

In the 1990s, graffiti continued but there was also an explosion in street art around the world. Some artists wanted to make political points and produced art that tried to make people think about war, inequality and discrimination. Other street artists were more concerned with producing beautiful, attractive work. In South America, many street artists went to work in poor areas adding colour, life and beauty to grey, city walls.

Social media, magazines, and shop windows constantly show people things to buy, and British shoppers are buying more clothes and shoes than ever. Online shopping makes it easy to buy without thinking, and big brands sell cheap clothes that people often wear just a few times before throwing them away.

Many people in Berlin, Germany, said that shooting pigs was too cruel. This caused strong arguments between hunters and animal lovers. In response to the protests, the city council chose to take a kinder approach to deal with the pigs. Instead of shooting them, they built fences and made it illegal to feed the pigs. We will see if this plan works, but it might be difficult because warmer winters mean there are more pigs now than before.

An important inspiration for the Hunger Games book comes from Suzanne's love of classical Greek mythology. When she was a child, one of her favourite stories was Theseus and the Minotaur. In this story the city of Athens is ruled by Crete, but the Athenians rebel. As a punishment, Minos the king of Crete forces the Athenians to send seven boys and seven girls to Crete every year. The youths are thrown into the labyrinth and eaten by a monster that lives there called the Minotaur. But one of the youths, named Theseus, fights the Minotaur and kills it. Suzanne sees Katniss Everdeen as a futuristic Theseus.

By bringing people and animals together, zoos have the potential to educate the public about conservation issues and inspire people to protect animals and their habitats. Some zoos provide a safe environment for animals which have been mistreated in circuses, or pets which have been abandoned. Zoos also carry out important research into subjects like animal behaviour and how to treat illnesses.

A new trend is growing against consumerism called the 'buy nothing' trend. It started in Canada in the early 1990s and then spread to the US. This trend is a response to the overspending during Black Friday and Cyber Monday after Thanksgiving. On Buy Nothing Day, people hold protests and cut up their credit cards. Throughout the year, Buy Nothing groups help people exchange and repair items they already have.

Is graffiti art or vandalism? This depends on your point of view, but in many countries, writing or painting on public or private property is considered vandalism. Many street artists have been stopped by the police and some have had to pay fines. Many city councils complain about the high cost of cleaning graffiti off buildings, buses and trains.

What does the art world think about graffiti and street art? Recently, more people are recognizing it as a real art form. There have been big exhibitions of street art in galleries in Paris, London, and Los Angeles. In 2008, American artist Elura Emerald organized a street art exhibition in a New York gallery. She supported street artists by saying, "Artists who paint on the street are just expressing themselves and not hurting anyone. They should be appreciated and celebrated."

If most people have four to six dreams every night after the age of ten, that's as many as 2,000 dreams per year. So, by the time they reach 80 years old the average person might have had 140,000 dreams. Even if we forget 95–99 per cent of our dreams, that's still a few thousand remembered dreams across a lifetime. It's not too difficult to believe that, by coincidence, a dream event is followed by a real-life event that's similar to it, especially if the subject of the dream is something that happens often in everyday life.

The Hunger Games takes place in the future, after the destruction of North America. The country is called Panem and is made up of twelve poor districts governed by the wealthy Capitol. The Capitol holds absolute power over the nation. Each district is responsible for producing different things for the Capitol. District 12, where the story begins, provides all the coal for the country. There used to be a thirteenth district but they rebelled against the Capitol in the past and were destroyed.

Often wild animals come into cities to look for food. In Cape Town, South Africa, baboons have started coming into residential areas on the edge of the city to feed. They open rubbish bins and eat fruit from gardens and orchards. Some brave baboons have even come into people's houses and taken food from kitchen cupboards and fridges! Baboons can be aggressive and have attacked a lot of pet animals, so understandably, many city residents don't welcome their presence.

Many bridge accidents happen while the bridge is being built. These accidents often happen because of mistakes made by the engineers, like wrong calculations. The bridge can fall down because it is too heavy, which can be very dangerous for the workers on it.

George Lucas was one of the early film directors to directly base his story on the 17 stages of the hero's journey. Typically the hero starts the story living an ordinary life, but something happens that calls them to an adventure that changes everything. At the beginning of Star Wars, Luke lives an ordinary life with his aunt and uncle, repairing robots. When he finds Princess Leia's message to Obi-Wan Kenobi inside the robot R2D2, it is 'the call to adventure' that starts the hero on his journey.

One idea to protect Earth from an asteroid is to use a nuclear weapon to blow it up. This can sound like a movie story, like in the 1998 film Armageddon, but it is a real plan from NASA called the Hypervelocity Asteroid Mitigation Mission for Emergency Response (HAMMER). The plan involves launching eight-ton rockets at an asteroid that is coming towards Earth, hoping to change its path. If the asteroid is too close for this to work, the rockets will have nuclear bombs to destroy it instead.

Campbell says that at first, the hero does not want to go on an adventure. Then, a mentor comes to help them, and they choose to enter a new world where the adventure takes place. Next, the hero faces tests, fights enemies, and meets friends to get ready for their biggest challenge. For Luke, his mentor is Obi-Wan, his friends are Han Solo and the robots R2D2 and C3PO, and his enemy is Darth Vader in the special world of the Death Star.

Items that are not used much might seem useless to some people, but they can be valuable to others. With the rise of the internet, online communities have found ways to make money by sharing these underused items. Websites and social media groups help people buy and sell second-hand goods, making it easier for people to share with each other. This is called the sharing economy.

In the 18th and 19th centuries, two main ideas about dreams became popular. One idea was that dreams show things we do not know about ourselves. Freud thought that if we understand our dreams, we can learn about our hidden feelings and the problems they cause. The other idea was different. It said that dreams are just random activity in the brain while it organizes memories and events from the day. When we wake up, we try to understand these random images and feelings and turn them into a story.

Religion is important to Pi. Though his family is Hindu, he is curious about other religions and he makes friends with a Christian priest and a Muslim baker. Some people believe that writing down your dreams can help you have lucid dreams. Lucid dreams are when you know you are dreaming and can control what happens in your dream. People might not realise they are part of the disposable clothing problem because they donate their unwanted clothes to charities. But charity shops can't sell all those unwanted clothes. 'Fast fashion' goes out of fashion as quickly as it came in and is often too poor quality to recycle; people don't want to buy it second-hand. Huge quantities end up being thrown away, and a lot of clothes that charities can't sell are sent abroad, causing even more economic and environmental problems.

Not content with one amazing trip, some of today's adventurers go from challenge to challenge. Meagan McGrath from Canada has climbed the highest mountain on each continent, ridden a bike across Canada and run a long-distance race in the Sahara Desert in 45ºC heat. But perhaps her most remarkable journey was a skiing trip to the South Pole. On the first day, she fell into a glacier and had to be rescued. Many of us would have given up at that point, but Meagan decided to carry on. She reached the South Pole forty days later, having pulled a sledge with a tent and all her food behind her through freezing conditions and ice storms.

Blek le Rat started out painting rats on the walls of his home city, Paris. Nowadays, he tries to make people think about different social issues and problems. He paints pictures of homeless people in big cities to encourage residents to think about the problem of homelessness.

In some areas, councils have tried to encourage artists not to paint graffiti randomly on walls by allowing them to work in designated areas. Taiwan is one such place and there are 'graffiti zones' where artists are free to paint and write on walls. In São Paulo in Brazil, the city council has even allowed some graffiti artists to paint on the city's subway trains.

Faith47 is from Cape Town in South Africa. She paints big, colourful pictures of people and animals and likes to explore different locations. Her work is found on pavements, in empty factories and on abandoned cars. She likes the fact that most street art is temporary and will soon be removed by weather or cleaners from the city council. For her, this reflects how life is full of change with its cycle of endings and new beginnings.

In her last job, Gabriela worked in a culture where people respected power and authority, and everyone had their own role. In this culture, leaders made important decisions and were rarely questioned. but, her Swedish team was used to a different culture where employees often worked with their bosses to solve problems and make decisions. In this environment, leaders acted like coaches or mentors, encouraging independent thinking and welcoming challenges.

When Gabriela became aware of the cultural differences between her and her team, she took the initiative to have an open conversation with them about their feelings about her leadership. Pleased to be asked for their thoughts, Gabriela's team openly expressed that they were not used to being told what to do. They enjoyed having more room for initiative and creative freedom. When she told her team exactly what she needed them to do, they felt that she didn't trust them to do their job well. They realised that Gabriela was taking it personally when they tried to challenge or make changes to her decisions, and were able to explain that it was how they'd always worked.

Os Gêmeos are identical twin brothers from São Paulo. They paint everything from tags to huge, colourful pictures of people on the sides of buildings. Their work is often so big that they need cranes to help them work. In 2007, they covered the whole of a castle in Scotland with paint.

People have been painting and writing on walls throughout history. In prehistoric times, people in Africa and Europe used to paint pictures of animals and people in caves. Graffiti has been found on buildings at ancient sites in Greece, Italy, Syria and Iraq. In the Roman town of Pompeii, archaeologists have found numerous examples of graffiti written in Latin. These include religious, political and romantic messages, and even some magic spells!

Have you ever dreamt of climbing Mount Everest or walking to the South Pole? If so, you're not alone. Every year, thousands of people try to climb the world's highest mountains or walk across continents. Unlike the explorers of the past who used maps and compasses, today's adventurers travel with modern technology like GPS and satellite phones. Many adventurers are nature lovers who use their travels to help raise awareness about a range of environmental issues, while others are keen to help people in need and raise money for charities.

We cannot know for sure how street art will change in the future, but we can see some trends. Most street artists are young people who create art in their cities or neighborhoods. However, more artists are now traveling and working in different countries. Many artists are also using the internet to communicate and share pictures of their work. Additionally, the art world is starting to recognize street art as a real form of art. Even though we are unsure about the future of street art, we can be confident that it will continue to exist!

Suzanne Collines has always found news programmes of wars upsetting. When she was a child, her father was a pilot in the US Air Force and he fought in Vietnam. Her mother tried to protect her by not telling her what was happening in the war, but she still saw news programmes about the war and knew that her dad was there. It was a very frightening experience for her.

Erik Weihenmayer from the United States is a multi-adventurer. He's ridden a bike through the deserts of Morocco, kayaked through the Grand Canyon and climbed Everest. Amazingly, Erik has been blind since the age of 13. Apart from his travels, he tries to encourage people with disabilities to live active lives and takes groups of young blind people on climbing expeditions.

Online platforms are giving people the chance to make some quick money. But now, with online marketplaces, they can easily sell baby clothes that were only worn a few times, or expensive pushchairs and equipment that their children no longer need. This way, they can earn back some of the money they spent.

She liked this time of day too because she could play with her pet rats.

Having decided to go to school, Auggie then has to face his first day. Like every child starting at a new school, he is really anxious. But because of the way he looks, it's an agonising experience. Nobody wants to sit next to him and he notices other kids staring at him or talking about him behind their hands. Fortunately, he makes friends with Jack, a boy in his class, and Summer, a girl he chats with at lunch. But it's not just the first day that's hard. Auggie soon learns that his classmates don't want to touch him for fear of catching 'the plague'. As he goes through the school year, Auggie goes through many intense ups and downs till finally an unexpected and traumatic event at a school camp changes things completely.

Over 4,000 climbers, aged from thirteen to eighty have been to the top of Everest. Though climbing high mountains in freezing conditions and violent storms is still extremely dangerous, the world's best climbers now look for new challenges. Gerlinde Kaltenbrunner from Austria fell in love with mountain climbing as a teenager. When she left school, she worked as a nurse, but kept climbing in her free time.

Having climbed Everest, Gerlinde decided to climb all fourteen of the world's 8,000 metre peaks. To increase the challenge, Gerlinde climbs without using oxygen tanks. This is risky as low oxygen levels at the top of high mountains can affect brain and body functioning. Gerlinde uses her fame as a climber to support a charity for poor children and orphans in Nepal.

If we look at the things we have bought in our lives, we will see that not everything is used often. For example, a thick wool coat that looked fashionable, even though we live in a hot country,  a smartphone that we stopped using after buying the newest model, a car that we only drive on weekends, or even a guest room in the house that slowly became a storeroom.

Throughout history and across cultures, dreams have been associated with prophecy. People thought dreams were messages from the gods, sent to give us knowledge or insight. Even today, many people can recall a time they dreamed about an event, place or person and then, later, the dream came true in real life.

Some of the largest and most costly transportation projects in the world are about building bridges. Bridges are important connections that allow cars, trucks, and trains to cross rivers, deep valleys, or other roads. Because of this, they are a key part of civil engineering and are closely examined, especially when they fall down.

After weeks of feeling frustrated, Gabriela emailed her Swedish manager about the problems she was having with her team. Her manager asked her if she thought her team was still doing well and what could help her work better with her team members. Gabriela thought her manager was unclear and did not feel he was handling the situation well.

Dogs that live in groups have learned that humans often give food to smaller, cuter dogs. So, these smaller dogs are sent to ask for food for the whole group. Some dogs have even figured out how to use the metro system to move around their area! Scientists are not sure how the dogs know when to get off the train. One idea is that they use their strong sense of smell to recognize the scents of places they like. Another idea is that they can understand the names of stations from the announcements. Now, metro passengers are so used to seeing dogs on the trains that they often don’t notice them.

Ed Stafford from the UK is the first person to walk the length of the Amazon River. He started by a small stream in the Andes mountains of Peru and arrived at the river's mouth in Brazil, two years and four months later, having walked 6,000 kilometres. The Amazon rainforest is home to poisonous snakes, crocodiles and jaguars, so Ed was in constant danger. Luckily, he survived with nothing worse than a few thousand mosquito and ant bites.

In Britain, the average person spends more than £1,000 on new clothes a year, which is around four per cent of their income. That might not sound like much, but that figure hides two far more worrying trends for society and for the environment. First, a lot of that consumer spending is via credit cards. British people currently owe approximately £670 per adult to credit card companies. That's 66 per cent of the average wardrobe budget. Also, not only are people spending money they don't have, they're using it to buy things they don't need. Britain throws away 300,000 tons of clothing a year, most of which goes into landfill sites.

Ed's walk would have been impossible without technology. He used a radio to ask the people of the rainforest for food and permission to cross their land. Many of them came to meet him and helped guide him through the most difficult terrain. As he walked Ed wrote a blog, recording his day-to-day experiences. He used the media interest in his trip to protest about the destruction of the rainforest and raise money for environmental and children's charities in Brazil and Peru.

Businesses have realized that they can make money from the sharing economy by using resources that are not fully used. A popular business model now is for companies to create online platforms that connect customers with people who can offer a specific product or service. For example, Airbnb helps people rent out their empty rooms and houses as profitable places to stay. Another example is Uber, which allows people to use their own cars as taxis to earn extra money in their free time.

One of the main roles of zoos today is to help with breeding programs for endangered animals. In the wild, some rare animals have trouble finding partners to breed with. They also face dangers from poachers, losing their homes, and other predators. A good zoo allows these animals to live and breed safely. As some wild animal numbers decrease, there is a risk that their populations become too similar genetically. Breeding programs help by allowing zoo-bred animals to be released into the wild, which increases genetic diversity.

Both types of accidents are very rare, but boats and trains can cause a bridge to fall for different reasons. For trains, it is the speed of the impact that can make a bridge collapse. For boats, it is their heavy weight that can cause the collapse, even if they are moving slowly. The best way to prevent bridge failures is to plan for them. New technologies that can find weak spots, safer working conditions, and better designs can all help to reduce these serious accidents.

At first, Pi is terrified of the animals and jumps into the ocean. One by one, the animals in the lifeboat kill and eat each other, till only Pi and the tiger are left. Tragically, Pi's family and the ship's sailors all drown, but Pi finds himself in a lifeboat with a hyena, zebra, orang-utan and an enormous tiger.

The Hunger Games is a hugely successful book for teenagers and young adults by the American author Suzanne Collins. It is also the first book for young readers to sell more than a million electronic copies. The Hunger Games is now a major Hollywood film and is just as successful. The rover analyses the air around it periodically, and in 2014 it found the air contained another of the most basic organic molecules and a key ingredient of natural gas: methane. One of the characteristics of methane is that it only survives a few hundred years. This means that something, somewhere on Mars, is replenishing the supply. According to NASA, Mars emits thousands of tons of methane at a time. The level of methane rises and falls at seasonal intervals in the year, almost as if the planet is breathing it.

Early in her career, the psychologist Carol Dweck of Stanford University gave a group of ten-year-olds problems that were slightly too hard for them. One group reacted positively, said they loved challenge and understood that their abilities could be developed. She says they had a 'growth mindset' and are focused on what they can achieve in the future. But another group of children felt that their intelligence was being judged and they had failed. They had a 'fixed mindset' and were unable to imagine improving. Some of these children said they might cheat in the future; others looked for someone who had done worse than them to boost their self-esteem.

Horror films love uninhabited places. This could be an abandoned hospital, a scary empty house or a ghost town. There's something about lonely, empty places. What was it like when people lived there? Why did they leave? Maybe it's also that they are so quiet, which can be very scary too. Of course, abandoned places are also handy for horror film directors in that it's more believable that you will have no phone coverage there either.

No matter what kind of house it is, the basement is a scary place in horror films. That's usually where something is hiding or where the evil psychopath has hidden their tools. Basements are always dark and often damp. You can only reach them by a narrow staircase. And basements are always creepy, even when there isn't anything down there.

Between the end of World War II and 1990, there were 30 wars that killed more than 100,000 people. Today there are still civil wars, but countries are mostly co-existing more peacefully than in the past. However, terrorism has shot up in the last few years and, since World War II, wars have killed many more civilians than soldiers. Even for civilians, though, the statistics are not all bad. Although deaths are nine times more likely to be a result of violent crime than political conflict, the global murder rate fell slightly, from 8 per 100,000 people in 2000 to about 5.3 in 2015.

Wasfia has dedicated her life to supporting human rights. She has seen many international projects in her country that help educate and train women and girls. However, when these projects end, many women and girls are left with nothing. Wasfia realized that Bangladesh needed to stand up for itself. She combined her two passions, climbing mountains and human rights, to change how people think about women in her country. She started climbing while working on humanitarian projects in Tibet and Nepal, because in Bangladesh, which is mostly flat and by the coast, many people have never seen a mountain. Her campaign is working, as more people in her country and around the world are starting to pay attention.

Many people think that developing countries are in a very bad place, facing extreme poverty, ruled by dictators, and having little chance for change. However, this is not true. In fact, a big change is happening. In the last 20 years, more than 700 million people have raised their income and escaped poverty. Also, six million fewer children die each year from diseases, more girls are going to school, and many more people have clean water.

Many managers try to make their feedback more positive by placing negative comments between two positive ones. if this becomes a habit, employees may start to see positive comments as just a way to soften the negative ones. Positive feedback should not just be used to cover up negative points; it should be given to support and encourage good performance.

I am part of the Campaign to Stop Killer Robots. Forget the scary image of a Terminator from movies. Right now, military machines like drones and robots are already being used to kill with little human control. The next step could be robots that can decide who to kill by themselves. I believe this would be very wrong and dangerous for people. We need to be very careful about what we let machines do.

Overall, more people are learning English than the other languages combined and English is spoken in the highest number of countries. However, Chinese has by far the greatest number of native speakers. There seems to be little correlation between how many native speakers there are of a language and the number of learners, but there is a stronger link between the number of learners and how many countries have speakers.

Your manager stops you and says she wants to talk about your work on the recent project. You feel worried all weekend, thinking about what you can have done wrong. When you go into her office on Monday morning, she starts by complimenting you on the good work you did on the project. You start to wonder if this is just the usual way to give feedback, which is called the 'feedback sandwich.' You know how it works: first, say something nice, then say what you really want to say, and finally, say something nice again.

Born in the USA is a fast rock album with strong rhythms, but its lyrics also convey deep feelings. Behind the catchy music are stories about the dark side of the American dream. Many songs talk about the hard lives of working people and their anger when life does not give them money or successs. For example, Glory Days is about small-town people remembering their youth, while Downbound Train tells of a young man whose life falls apart after losing his job. It is easy to think the singer is using the voice of the real people he knew, and the life he might have lived without fame. The album clearly shows the great talent of "the boss".

At the beginning the girl is usually innocent, shy and not particularly strong. By the end, she has become the toughest and most resourceful person in the world. The last girl almost always wins in the end.

To understand where our ability to use complex language comes from, we need to look at how our brains are different from those of other animals. It is not just about brain size; we also need to consider what other functions our brains have and how they developed over time. There are very few physical clues to help us; the tools left by our ancestors do not show us what kind of speech they could make. However, we can see changes in the mouth, throat, and tongue of early humans. By around 100,000 years ago, humans had developed the ability to make complex sounds. Before that, scientists can only guess if early humans used simpler sounds to communicate.

Society, not nature, tells us that girls should like arts and humanities, while boys should focus on maths and physics. Also, there are not many positive female role models in science jobs for young people to see. Cartoons and stories often show scientists, inventors, or astronauts as men. There is also a wrong idea that scientists are nerdy, have bad social skills, or that their work is lonely and separate from the world. These stereotypes from the media can make girls feel they do not belong in science and see it as an unattractive career. If girls had more positive female role models in science, it would help them feel more confident and included in those subjects.

The Scallion is printed weekly and distributed free in faculty buildings, with a readership of approximately 10,000 students. It is written and produced entirely by students. The survey shows that the newspaper is highly valued by university students and staff for entertainment, cultural enrichment and work experience. The cost of printing newspapers is significant. Furthermore, some students do not have easy access to the paper, since the only way to obtain a copy is to physically go to university. An additional environmental issue is that a large number of copies end up as litter on campus.

At Girox Foods, we have an annual employee turnover of about 12 percent. This may not seem high, but the average in our industry is seven percent. The main goal of this report is to find out why employees are engaged in their work and to suggest ways to improve their experience at the company and keep them longer.

What the speaker said felt very true to me. I really believe that the more connected we are, the more alone we can feel. This is not a big problem for my generation, as we have lived without technology for a long time. We know how to be alone and understand that it's okay to be alone. But for people under 20, it's different. They are so busy talking online that they don’t know what it feels like to be alone and might not learn how to enjoy their own company. Also, they are learning to talk through messages that can be changed, instead of learning how to have real conversations with people face to face.
